description: Incorporating Climate Change Adaptation into the Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument Management Plan is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Climate Adaptation Knowledge Exchange (CAKE); NOAA, National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration; State of Hawai'i Department of Land and Natural Resources. The Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument (PMNM) is situated in the northwestern portion of the Hawaiian Archipelago and is one of the world’s largest marine protected areas. Management of the Monument is the responsibility of four co-trustees: the State of Hawaii Department of Land and Natural Resources; Office of Hawaiian Affairs; the U.S. Coverage: Northwestern Hawaiian Islands (2008). The toolkit gives Northwestern Hawaiian Islands as the location, 2008 as the year and 8 years as the duration. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
